main_body: A 4x3-tile ground patch of mid-green grass with sparse dark-green clumps and small tuft marks. The same 16px tile pattern repeats across the whole patch.
top_band: none (flat terrain tiles, so there is no standing volume and no top/front split)
evidence: This is a terrain ground surface, not a standing object, so the 3/4 top-plus-front contract does not apply. It has no receding side faces and is not drawn as an elevation of an object. Nothing in it fails the view contract.

style.evidence: The ground is mostly one mid-green with a dark-green blob, a few darker tuft pixels and rare light dots, so only about 3-4 tones. The Beodeul grass reference has several greens, with layered tufts and visible grain. Large areas of 5x5 pixels or more are one flat colour. The same motif repeats identically every 16px, which makes the tiling obvious. Each tile carries only about 4 colours, well below the reference's richness. The overall contrast is low and the surface reads as thinner and flatter than the reference.
